decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left approach toward the gray nut, lifting and gradually turning downward; right arm stays home. Nut location estimated from head RGB.
Continue left elbow-up arc to a downward-facing hover over the gray nut. Maintain clearance before descending.
Lower the open left gripper around the gray nut, with a small head-image alignment correction. Stop at estimated side-grasp height.
Fine-center on the gray nut using wrist RGB, close fully, then lift vertically to check retention.
Gray nut is retained in the wrist view. Carry it above its gray screw and lower slightly toward the thread entrance; keep fully closed.
Make a millimetric wrist-image centering correction, seat the gray nut, and begin a slow clockwise threading turn with slight axial descent.
Release the gray nut on the screw, reset wrist yaw without unwinding it, then regrasp for another tightening stroke.
The gray nut slipped beside the screw during release. Open, clear the screw, and approach the fallen nut for a more carefully centered retry.
Center and lower around the displaced gray nut, close fully, and lift a short distance for visual retention confirmation.
Retention is uncertain. Reopen and descend to a lower side-grasp on the gray nut, then close without translating.
The nut shifted during closure. Raise open fingers, realign over its current head-image center, and restore a vertical approach before retrying.
Use the wrist image to center the nut between the fingers, descend to its side walls, close fully and lift for retention inspection.
Gray nut appears held. Lift clear and align above the gray screw; pause above the tip for wrist-camera centering before insertion.
Lower the gray nut onto the centered screw tip, then turn clockwise while following the thread downward. Keep closed until seating is visually confirmed.
Gray screw now fills the nut opening. Release and withdraw to inspect retention, then move the left arm above the blue nut with an open gripper.
Gray pair remains together after release. Align the left gripper over the blue nut and descend open to its side-grasp height.
Fine-center the blue nut between the fingers, close fully at side-grasp height, and lift vertically to verify retention.
Carry the retained blue nut toward a central table handoff location, staying on the left side with the right arm parked.
Place the blue nut upright at the center-front handoff point and open the left fingers. The right arm remains clear until the left retreats.
Withdraw the empty left gripper upward and left. Begin a separated elbow-up approach with the right arm for the central blue nut.
Park the left arm farther left while finishing the right wrist's downward orientation and approaching the center handoff from the right.
Move the right hand over the central blue nut and descend open, keeping the left arm parked clear. Inspect wrist alignment before closing.
Lower the right fingers to the blue nut's side walls, close fully, then lift slightly to test retention before transport.
The blue nut is visibly retained. Lift for clearance and carry it rightward above the matching blue screw, keeping the left arm parked.
Use the right wrist view to correct the blue nut toward the screw axis, then lower carefully to the thread entrance while keeping the grip closed.
The blue screw is left of the held nut in the wrist view. Correct that offset with small motions and lower a few millimeters; do not release yet.
Fine-center the blue screw tip in the nut bore, seat it with a shallow descent, and make a clockwise threading stroke while holding closed.
The blue shaft is visible but slightly offset in the bore. Make a small wrist-frame centering correction and continue a shallow clockwise tightening stroke.
The blue nut appears tilted against the screw rather than seated. Lift clear while retaining it, reset wrist yaw, and correct the inferred fore-aft axis offset before retrying.
Test a slow straight descent at the corrected blue axis without twisting. Nut tilt and insertion remain uncertain, so stop for another wrist view.
Correct the blue nut's fore-aft offset toward the visible screw, with a small clearance lift before lowering. Avoid further twisting while the bore is unseated.
The blue screw tip is now visible inside the bore. Lower slowly to engage it, then apply a small clockwise tightening stroke while following downward.
Blue nut is not seated and has shifted in the fingers. Lift clear and move to an unobstructed right-side table area to restore an upright grasp.
Set the blue nut down on a clear table patch and release it so its flat base can settle upright before a centered regrasp.
Recenter the right fingers over the settled blue nut, take a lower side-wall grasp, and lift slightly to check that it is upright and retained.
The blue nut is upright in the new grasp. Carry it back above the matching screw with clearance and stop for fresh axis alignment.
Blue nut and screw appear laterally aligned. Lower straight and slowly to the thread entrance, maintaining the upright grasp and checking before any rotation.
The upright blue nut now surrounds the screw tip. Seat a few millimeters deeper and apply a controlled clockwise turn, keeping both arms on their own sides.
Release and withdraw from the blue pair to check whether it remains seated. Reset the empty right wrist and begin approaching the red nut from the right.
The blue pair remains together after withdrawal. Approach the red nut from the right at clearance height, then descend to an open-gripper hover for alignment.
The last approach stopped on an IK continuity guard. Replan from the observed pose: lower with much smaller inward increments to recover reach margin and inspect the red nut alignment.
Fine-align the open right gripper toward the red nut using the wrist image, with a shallow descent and small increments near the central reach boundary.
Center the red nut between the right fingers, close at side-wall height, and lift slightly outward to verify retention while easing the central reach.
The red nut is visibly retained. Carry it outward and upward toward its matching red screw, with the left arm parked and clearance for fresh alignment.
Red screw tip appears centered under the held nut. Lower slowly to engage the thread and start a gentle clockwise turn, without releasing.
Continue the red nut's clockwise tightening stroke with a shallow axial descent, then pause to inspect seating before any release.
Red seating is uncertain and the nut appears tilted. Open and lift clear to inspect its resting position, then reset the empty wrist for a better-centered grasp.
The red nut fell beside the screw. Reapproach its current upright position with an open, vertical gripper for a centered side-wall grasp.
Fine-center the red nut from the wrist image, descend to its side walls, close fully, then lift a short distance to verify an upright grasp.
The red nut is upright in the new grasp. Lift clear, move above its matching screw, and stop just above the thread entrance for visual alignment.
The regrasped red nut is upright and centered over the screw. Lower onto the tip, then turn clockwise with slight axial descent while maintaining the grasp.
Release and lift away from the red pair to inspect whether the nut stays upright on the screw. Reset the empty wrist only after clearing the part.
Red nut did not remain on the screw. Reapproach its new table position for a centered grasp; next insertion will use a straight descent before twisting.
Fine-center on the displaced red nut and close at side-wall height. Lift vertically for another upright-retention check before moving toward the screw.
Lift the retained red nut clear of the screw, then approach its axis using a slightly corrected head-image position. Pause above contact for wrist alignment.
Lower the red nut straight down at one millimeter per step without twisting. Inspect whether the screw enters the bore before applying any more torque-like rotation.
The red tip is now inside the bore with no table visible through it. Complete a small seating descent, then turn clockwise slowly while keeping the upright nut captured.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Release the apparently seated red nut, withdraw vertically, and reset the empty wrist away from the parts.
All three color pairs remain together after release. Begin returning both empty arms toward their origins along separated elbow-up arcs, keeping the grippers open.
Finish the gradual return to each arm's original pose with open grippers. The three assembled pairs remain on the table, clear of the retreat paths.
Make the final submillimeter origin correction and hold both empty grippers open, allowing the assembled pairs and robot to settle.
Hold at origin with both grippers open and observe whether all three seated color-matched assemblies remain stable.
Maintain the returned origin poses with open grippers. All three matched assemblies remain stable in RGB; avoid disturbing them while the episode continues.
Keep both arms at origin with open grippers. The three color-matched assemblies remain upright and stable; no further contact is planned.
Hold the returned origin poses with both grippers open. All three matched pairs remain stable in RGB; avoid disturbing the seated nuts.
Continue holding at origin with open grippers while observing the three stable, color-matched assemblies.
Maintain both origin poses with open grippers. The three matched assemblies remain stable; continue observing without disturbing them.
The pairs are stable, but final thread depth remains uncertain. Reapproach gray with the left arm and blue with the right for controlled additional tightening, using separated elbow-up arcs.
Finish downward-facing hovers over the seated gray and blue nuts. Keep open and above contact for fresh wrist alignment before additional tightening.
Gray appears flush, so leave it untouched. Regrasp the blue nut at its current seated height for additional clockwise tightening; keep the left gripper open and clear.
Tighten the captured blue nut clockwise through a controlled stroke with only a small downward follow. Leave the flush gray assembly untouched.
Release and reset the right wrist without unwinding the blue nut, then regrasp slightly lower for another tightening stroke. Withdraw the empty left arm from the gray pair.
Apply another clockwise blue-nut stroke with minimal axial follow. Begin returning the empty left arm toward home along its separate elbow-up path.
Finish the empty left arm's return to origin. Release and reset the right wrist without unwinding the seated blue nut, then regrasp for another short tightening pass.
Apply another clockwise blue-nut stroke without further downward pressure. Settle the empty left arm at its original pose and keep it open.
Continue the blue nut clockwise within the wrist range, with only two millimeters of axial follow, then open to inspect its seated depth.
Blue remains on its screw after release. Raise the open fingers slightly to the nut's side-wall level and reset yaw before a better-centered final tightening pass.
